analysis:
The changed file is test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift). Head-side changes: StubTokenizer gains a decodeTable (lines ~146-155); makeBridge gains a stopStringScope parameter (~440, 459); new tests at 844-896 cover scoped matched-stop-sequence reporting (ReasoningStopScope with qwen3 and gemma4), request-scope versus model-scope precedence, and EOS rendering not impersonating a stop string. No production code is changed in the supplied units, so no controls were weakened.

Relevant existing assertions I checked:
- bridgeStampsCacheSalt (lines 758-782) still asserts that cacheSalt comes only from the coordinator-supplied cacheScope. Caller-controlled prompt_cache_key and user stay nil. This supports the T-041 mitigation for authenticated, coordinator-authored cache scoping. It is unchanged in this PR and is exercised by tests only.
- The usageMaxDefense test (1059-1070) asserts that terminal usage can only raise the observed counts, which defends against billing-zero.
- The engine error test (1103-1122) asserts that telemetry never carries the raw engine message in fixed keys.
- The retired-env test (1679-1707) shows the SSD envs DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_DISK_GB and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL are live, consistent with the T-041 description.

Open question for integration: the production implementation of the new scoped matchedStopSequence and ReasoningStopScope (EngineV2Bridge) is not in the supplied units. Any correctness or security effect of stop-string scoping on output truncation or billing usage cannot be assessed from tests alone. This is a limited-coverage note, not a finding. The test file adds no attack surface.
